entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since mid-October 2026):

---

- 
**New GRPM Anishinaabek exhibit opened Oct. 13, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum unveiled its reimagined "$5 million" exhibit "Anishinaabek: The Original People of This Place" on Indigenous Peoples Day, Oct. 13, 2026, replacing a gallery that had been part of the museum since 1994 and featuring immersive environments, multimedia storytelling, hologram experiences, a Veterans Wall of Honor, and newly commissioned Anishinaabe artworks.
 (Spectrum News / Grand Rapids Magazine)

- 
**Tribal co-development process for GRPM exhibit confirmed:** The new Anishinaabek exhibit was developed in partnership with the Eshtoojik Council, an advisory group representing Michigan's federally and state-recognized tribal governments; council members worked with museum staff beginning in 2023 to review content and provide cultural guidance.
 (Grand Rapids Magazine, Oct. 12, 2026)

- 
**H.R. 3255 (Grand River Bands Restoration Act) stalled in House Natural Resources Committee as of October 2026:** The Cherokee One Feather's October 2026 federal acknowledgment update confirms the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians are still pursuing recognition through Congress, with H.R. 3255 referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources and no scheduled hearing as of press time.
 (The Cherokee One Feather, Oct. 21, 2026)

- 
**Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids issue public call for GRB recognition, Sept. 16, 2026:** The Dominican Sisters formally announced support for reaffirming federal recognition of the Grand River Bands, stating that "the federal government's failure to recognize the Grand River Bands has too often rendered the Tribe invisible in public life despite its enduring history and identity."
 (Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids, Sept. 16, 2026)

- 
**Michigan Historical Commission to review GRB footpath marker language in November 2026:** The Commission is scheduled to meet this month to consider language for a historical marker to be installed in the Eastown neighborhood of Grand Rapids along the route of the ancestral Grand River Bands trade footpath.
 (Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians website)

- 
**Michigan Archaeology Day held Oct. 24, 2026 in Lansing:** The annual event at the Michigan History Museum included a talk using UM-Dearborn's River Raisin Archaeological Project to illuminate stories of French-descended settler families and lasting consequences for the Wyandot, Potawatomi, and other Nations of the "Old Northwest."
 (Michigan DNR / Michigan History Center, Oct. 13, 2026)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~October 10, 2026), plus a couple of closely adjacent developments that postdate the August 1, 2026 River Brain baseline:

---

- 
**Canal Park reopened Oct. 29, 2026:** Downtown Grand Rapids's Canal Park opened to visitors after a $9.9 million improvement project, funded through a combination of parks millage revenue, local tax authority funding, and grants.
 
The improvements cover more than half a mile of riverfront space and include a nature-themed playground, outdoor exercise equipment, wider pedestrian walkways, and a new accessible kayak launch (pulled for the season, reopening spring 2027).
 (WOOD TV / Yahoo News, Oct. 29, 2026)

- 
**Acrisure Amphitheater noise ordinance exemption, Oct. 27, 2026:** The Grand Rapids City Commission voted unanimously to exempt the Acrisure Amphitheater from the city's noise ordinance, overriding a Kent County Circuit Court ruling from August 2026 that had ordered the venue to comply with the ordinance.
 
The exemption allows the amphitheater to operate under its special land use permit, permitting noise above the city's ordinance levels from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., with potential for extensions.
 (WOOD TV, Fox 17, Michigan Public, Oct. 27-28, 2026)

- 
**Michigan Transformational Brownfield cap doubled, July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed legislation doubling the statewide cap on post-construction transformational brownfield tax captures from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, clearing a path for stalled projects including developments in downtown Grand Rapids.
 
SB 723 also removes the program's 2027 expiration date and expands the program to more communities across Michigan.
 
The Michigan Strategic Fund board subsequently approved new program guidelines in September 2026.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, July 22; WOOD TV, Sept. 23, 2026)

- 
**Acrisure Amphitheater nominated for national award:** After scheduling 43 shows from May through October 2026, the $184 million venue was nominated for National Amphitheater of the Year 2026 by the International Entertainment Buyers Association.
 (Experience GR, Oct. 2026)

- 
**Grand River Restoration Lower Reach construction began July 2026:** Construction of the first phase of the Grand River Restoration project (Lower Reach) started in July 2026, timed to protect fish spawning periods.
 
The adjacent renovation of Ah-Nab-Awen Park is expected to be completed in late fall 2026.
 (Experience GR, Oct. 2026)

- 
**Grand Action 2.0 pursuing $270 million high-rise south of Acrisure Amphitheater:** One week after the amphitheater's May 2026 opening, Grand Action 2.0 announced it was pursuing a $270 million, 21-story mixed-use development immediately

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Now let me do a targeted search for the most recent (last 30 days, October-November 2026) news to make sure nothing very recent is missed.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (October 10 to November 9, 2026). Items predating August 1, 2026 (the base research date) or already well-established are excluded.

---

- **DNR northern pike regulation change, effective Oct. 15, 2026:** 
The NRC enacted updated northern pike regulations, adjusting daily possession limits to allow harvesting smaller fish in select lakes and removing an unnecessary spawning closure.
 
Specifically, Otsego Lake pike marsh was reopened year-round, and Au Sable Lake (Ogemaw Co.), Clear Lake (Mecosta Co.), Gibson Lake (Iron Co.), and Hanbury Lake (Dickinson Co.) were added to the list of waters with a daily possession limit of up to five northern pike, with only one fish 24 inches or greater allowed.
 These changes are not reflected in the printed 2026 regulations; 
anglers must check the digital version at Michigan.gov/DNRRegs or in the Michigan DNR Hunt Fish app.
 (Oct. 15, 2026, Michigan DNR)

- **No current water advisories on the Grand River at Grand Rapids as of Nov. 9, 2026:** 
As of the last update on Nov. 9, 2026, no watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for the Grand River at Grand Rapids.
 (Nov. 9, 2026, NOAA National Water Prediction Service)

- **MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guide released June 8, 2026 (confirmed post-base):** 
MDHHS released the 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guides on June 8, 2026, covering 696 Michigan waterbodies; 60 guidelines were relaxed and 64 became more protective than previous years.
 Grand River-specific advisories in the Southwest Michigan guide continue to flag PFOS in bluegill, rock bass, and sunfish, and PCBs in carp. (June 8, 2026, MDHHS)

- **Sept. 10, 2026 NRC regulation changes to inland trout, salmon, and sturgeon (Fisheries Orders 254 and 205):** 
The NRC enacted regulation changes to Fisheries Orders 254 and 205 effective Sept. 10, 2026, clarifying possession limits, identifying current fish communities, and aligning certain fishing rules with Wisconsin.
 These are not reflected in the printed 2026 regulations. (Sept. 10, 2026, Michigan DNR)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (since ~October 10, 2026):

---

- **Lake sturgeon, sex-determination genetics, Sept. 30 2026:** 
Michigan researchers refined genetic testing that can more reliably determine the sex of lake sturgeon, particularly in young fish and outside the spawning season, with the breakthrough expected to reduce handling time and allow analysis of archived samples.
 (Great Lakes Commission / MLive)

- **Sea lamprey, Lake Michigan population count, Oct. 19 2026:** 
Sea lamprey populations declined in four of the five Great Lakes in 2026, including Lake Michigan, where the estimated adult population fell to 20,211, down from 21,273 in 2025.
 
The commission noted no statistically significant five-year trends were detected in any of the Great Lakes.
 (Great Lakes Fishery Commission / Mason County Press)

- **Snuffbox mussel, stocking event, Oct. 7 2026:** 
Michigan DNR biologists and federal partners placed thousands of endangered snuffbox mussels in suitable habitat across three Michigan waterways, with 1,000 of the stocked mussels tagged with unique physical identifiers glued to each shell.
 (Outdoor News)

- **Invasive species, New Zealand mudsnail first detection near Grand River watershed, Nov. 2 2026:** 
Michigan Invasive Species Program biologists are gathering information after detecting invasive New Zealand mudsnails in southern Michigan and will conduct additional sampling at the site and other Thornapple River tributaries in Barry, Kent, and Ionia counties; genetic testing will be used to attempt to identify source populations.
 
The brown-to-black, one-eighth-inch snail is prohibited in Michigan and all individuals are female, reproducing by cloning.
 (Michigan DNR)

- **DNR fish stocking, genetic tracking initiative, Oct. 15 2026:** 
The Michigan DNR has begun using genetic testing to track the success of fish-stocking operations, helping determine whether stocked fish are surviving in waterways.
 
For the upcoming fiscal year, the DNR will take 500 samples of stocked walleye from waterbodies across the state for genetic testing at a Michigan State University lab.
 (Michigan Public)

- **Salmon and steelhead run, Sixth Street weir counts, early Oct. 2026:** 
At the Sixth Street weir in Grand Rapids, coho counts surged from 28 on Oct. 6 to 233 on Oct. 7, with fall steelhead counts rising from 7 to 75 on those same dates.
 
As of Oct. 29, guide reports indicated steelhead anglers should stick to larger systems like the Grand and Muskegon, as tributary flows were low and stale fish needed a rain event to bring fresh fish upriver.
 (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub / Werkman Outfitters)

entries.title: Hydrology and weather
entries.body:
Here is what the searches returned that is genuinely current and relevant to the River Brain, as of today, Nov 9, 2026:

---

- 
**NWS gauge GDRM4, Grand River at Grand Rapids, as of Nov 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC: no watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect; the observed stage is reading approximately 1.50 ft, well below action stage of 12.0 ft.
 (NOAA Water Prediction, Nov 9, 2026)

- 
**NWS Grand Rapids climate summary for Nov 1, 2026** shows precipitation since Sep 1 at only 4.64 in, against a normal of 7.57 in, a deficit of 2.93 in, indicating the basin entered November running significantly below normal on accumulated precipitation.
 (NWS Grand Rapids Climate Report, Nov 2, 2026)

- 
**NWS North Central River Forecast Center product from Sep 21, 2026** recorded the Grand River at Grand Rapids (GDRM4) at 2.7 ft stage, with a 5-day forecast holding near 2.3 to 2.8 ft range, all well below action stage (12.0 ft); minor, moderate, and major flood thresholds at that gauge are 18.0, 21.0, and 23.0 ft respectively.
 (NWS NCRFC River Forecast, Sep 21, 2026)

- 
The NOAA gauge at Grand Rapids (GDRM4) confirmed **no watches, warnings, or advisories** in effect as of the Nov 9, 2026 update, consistent with persistently low autumn flow conditions.
 (NOAA Water Prediction, Nov 9, 2026)

**Note:** No new ice jam events, flooding episodes, drought declarations, or record readings for the Grand River at Grand Rapids were found in the last 30 days. The most recent significant hydrologic event in the record remains the **spring 2026 flood**, when the river reached approximately 15.45 ft (moderate flood stage) at Comstock Park on Apr 8, 2026, well before the Aug 1 base research date. Current conditions show low, calm autumn flow with a precipitation deficit and no active NWS advisories.

entries.body:
Now let me do one more targeted search to look for the most recent news (last 30 days, October-November 2026) on these topics.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found since August 1, 2026, based on sources dated within roughly the last 30 days (mid-October to November 9, 2026):

- **Lower Reach boulder placement and dam removal actively underway, first rapids audible.** As of late September 2026, crews from Taplin Group had installed a sandbag cofferdam, placed GPS-coordinated boulders near the Blue Bridge, and removed at least one low-head dam north of Gillett Bridge. 
Chapman reported crews began work July 1, with two of four dams expected removed by end of summer, and noted that "for the first time in over 100 years, you can actually hear rapids roaring in Downtown Grand Rapids."
 (Sep. 30, 2026, citizenportal.ai / Talking Michigan Transportation)

- **Construction Equipment Guide feature confirms two-season schedule ending fall 2027.** A trade-press site visit in early October documented a Komatsu excavator placing boulders in the river. 
Construction is expected to span two seasons and conclude in fall 2027, depending on water levels and weather, with a sandbag cofferdam serving as a water-control barrier across the river.
 (Oct. 7, 2026, Construction Equipment Guide)

- **Canal Park reopened October 29, 2026 after $9.9 million renovation.** 
Canal Park is now open to visitors following a $9.9 million improvement project; the updated park includes a nature-themed playground, outdoor exercise equipment, wider pedestrian walkways, and a new enclosed heated pavilion for community gatherings.
 This is the first completed Grand River Greenway amenity adjacent to the active Lower Reach work zone. (Oct. 29, 2026, WOOD TV / Yahoo News)

- **Sixth Street Dam EIS: draft expected July 2027, 14 alternatives under review.** No new EIS milestone was announced post-August; the most current confirmed status is: 
the Army Corps of Engineers officially resumed the EIS process in spring 2026, a draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027, and the public comment period closed May 22, 2026.
 Additionally, 
the EIS process will consider 14 different alternatives, some of which call for the removal of the Sixth Street Dam.
 No post-August update found. (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, grandriver.network)

- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park remains closed through project completion (est. 2027-2028); no reopening date set.** 
In May 2026, crews began staging equipment and materials in the park to prepare for Lower Reach in-river work, and the closure of Ah-Nab-Awen Park will continue through the project period.
 No change to closure status found in the past 30 days. (grandriver.network)

- **Fall 2026 in-river work window nearing close.** 
The active construction season runs roughly July through mid-October or early November each year, weather and river conditions permitting,
 meaning crews are at or near the end of Season 1 in-water work as of today, Nov. 9, 2026. No official end-of-season announcement found yet. (Spectrum News Michigan)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~October 3, 2026):

---

- **Sea lamprey, Lake Michigan, Oct. 19, 2026:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission reported that the estimated adult sea lamprey population in Lake Michigan declined to 20,211 in 2026, down from 21,273 in 2025, putting the annual estimate just below the management target of 20,526.
 
Overall, the sea lamprey population decreased by 25% across the Great Lakes this year.
 (Great Lakes Fishery Commission, Mason County Press)

- **Invasive species, new detection, Nov. 2, 2026:** 
Invasive New Zealand mudsnails were found in Bear Creek, a small coldwater tributary of the Thornapple River in Kent County, representing the first detection in the southern Lower Peninsula, approximately 75 miles south of the closest infestation in the Pere Marquette River; the snails were collected by Coldwater River Watershed Council volunteers during routine macroinvertebrate monitoring.
 (Michigan DNR, WOOD TV)

- **Salmon and steelhead run, late October 2026:** 
As of October 29, the salmon run was mostly winding down on the Grand River; tributaries were not producing, with guides recommending sticking to larger systems like the Grand and the Muskegon, and noting that fresh fish needed a bump in flows to move in.
 (Werkman Outfitters fishing report)

- **Lake sturgeon longevity study, published July 30, 2026:** 
A new study by researchers from the Michigan DNR, Michigan State University, Michigan Technological University, and the Wisconsin DNR suggests that lake sturgeon may live longer than the previously accepted maximum of 150 years, possibly much longer.
 
Using decades of capture-and-recapture records from five Great Lakes populations, researchers found that in some populations lake sturgeon may routinely live well beyond 200 years, with some approaching 300 years.
 (Michigan DNR Newsroom, Michigan in Pictures)

- **Snuffbox mussel critical habitat, April 24, 2026:** 
Four freshwater mussel species, including the snuffbox, received new federal protections when the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service designated over 3,800 miles of rivers as critical habitat across 17 states.
 
For the Grand River specifically, the designated snuffbox unit (SNBO 4) covers 41 river miles in Ionia and Kent Counties, extending from Webber Dam downstream to the confluence with the Thornapple River near Ada.
 (Federal Register, CBS Detroit)

- **Lake sturgeon research funding, 2026:** 
The six-year research partnership of GRPM, John Ball Zoo, GVSU, and Encompass Consulting was awarded a new grant from the Great Lakes Fishery Trust to support sonar technology for the detection of adult sturgeon, with the goal of documenting spawning migrations using non-invasive monitoring methods.
 (WGRD, GRPM Blog)

The stocking targeted the Huron and Clinton rivers and Cass Lake.
 
Per the October 7, 2026 report, 1,000 of the stocked mussels were tagged with unique physical ID tags glued to each shell.

 (Oct. 7, 2026, Construction Equipment Guide)

- **Upper Reach EIS timeline: design selection now estimated at 2028:** 
The Sixth Street Dam will not be removed until a new barrier is constructed; Lisa Walter, aquatic connectivity coordinator for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, stated the Army Corps EIS process means "we're looking at probably 2028 until we have a project design selected."
 
More than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier project.
 (July 31, 2026, Bridge Michigan / Capital News Service, the most recent sourced figure on EIS timeline)

- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park closure ongoing through project end:** 
The park will be closed for the next two years; specific closures include the riverwalk between Bridgewater Place and the north end of the park, the switchback path to the river's edge at Michigan Street, and the tunnel beneath the Gillette Bridge on the south end.
 No new reopening date or scope change found beyond what was established at closure. (May 28, 2026, WOOD TV, closure still in effect)
